routes.label: Find the total seconds, then convert

question: Casey’s shop class is making a golf trophy. He has to paint \(300\) dimples on a golf ball. If it takes him \(2\) seconds to paint one dimple, how many minutes will he need to do his job?
solution:
Each of the \(300\) dimples takes \(2\) seconds, so the total painting time is
\[
300\cdot2=600\text{ seconds}.
\]
Since one minute contains \(60\) seconds, this is
\[
600\div60=\boxed{10\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.* Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known. Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.) *Students need not use formal terms for these properties.

edges.reason: The equal-addend sum being rewritten as a product contains chained addition. The subtraction half of the endpoint is not required.
The target explicitly includes the multiplication-division relation, so multiplication meaning is needed for that inverse-operation assertion.
The minute-second conversion explicitly uses the relation sixty seconds equals one minute established by the two time units.

Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.
